headline: weak
texts: Several core areas need rebuilding. That is useful information, not a verdict. Start with the first review cards listed below, and retake the journey after a day.

Direct versus indirect is a gap. Rebuild it from the route: the indirect sac enters at the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; the direct sac bulges through the posterior wall, medial to them.
Hesselbach's triangle is a gap. Rebuild it from the inferior epigastric artery, lateral rectus border and inguinal ligament. Rings and the conjoint tendon are neighbours, not sides.
Inguinal versus femoral position is a gap. Femoral lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle, inguinal above and medial. Trace the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament.

Cause and clinical picture are a gap. Indirect is congenital, from a patent processus vaginalis, and follows the cord into the scrotum. Direct is acquired, from posterior wall weakness, and rarely reaches the scrotum.

The bedside tests are a gap. Occlusion of the deep ring controls an indirect sac while a direct sac still appears medial. In Zieman's test, index suggests indirect, middle direct, ring finger femoral.

The 'most common' answers are a gap. Indirect inguinal hernia is the commonest type overall, in both sexes and in children. Femoral is only relatively commoner in women, and a left sliding hernia most often contains sigmoid colon.

Strangulation risk is a gap. Indirect strangulates more than direct because of its narrow neck, and femoral is the highest-risk groin hernia. The scope word, inguinal or groin, decides which ranking applies.

First step and investigation are a gap. A strangulated hernia needs resuscitation and emergency surgery, never forceful taxis. An evident hernia needs no imaging; an occult one needs ultrasound first, then MRI if inconclusive.

Choosing the operation is a gap. Child: herniotomy alone. Adult open: Lichtenstein mesh repair, with older keys saying Bassini. Bilateral or recurrent after open: laparoscopic TEP or TAPP. Best tissue repair: Shouldice.

Nerves and triangles are a gap. Ilioinguinal is the nerve most injured in open repair; lateral femoral cutaneous in laparoscopic. The triangle of doom holds the external iliac vessels, the triangle of pain holds nerves.
The named hernias are shaky. Anchor each: Amyand is appendix in an inguinal sac, de Garengeot appendix in a femoral sac, Littre has a Meckel's diverticulum, Richter traps part of the wall.

You judged danger by the size of the swelling. Risk follows the neck: the indirect hernia's narrow neck at the deep ring strangulates more readily than the direct hernia's wide, diffuse bulge. Trace the neck first, then rank the two. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You answered the narrower inguinal ranking when the stem said 'groin'. Among all groin hernias, femoral has the highest risk of strangulation; indirect only wins when the stem says inguinal. Underline the scope word in every superlative stem. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You reused one famous nerve for both approaches without reading the setting word. Ilioinguinal is the nerve most often injured in open repair; the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is most at risk in laparoscopic repair, giving anterolateral thigh paraesthesia. Pair each nerve with its field of dissection. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You treated 'newer' as 'default' and chose laparoscopic repair without reading the qualifiers. Bilateral hernia and recurrence after open repair favour it; laparoscopic repair needs general anaesthesia and a learning curve, so a primary unilateral hernia without expertise stays open. Check the qualifiers first. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You memorised the occlusion test result without its mechanism, so it flipped. Pressure over the deep ring blocks the route of an indirect sac, which stays controlled on coughing; a direct sac comes through the posterior wall and still appears medial to the finger. Predict the sac's exit before choosing. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You recalled fingertip rules by rote order rather than by anatomy. In Zieman's test the index finger sits over the deep ring (indirect), middle over the superficial ring (direct), ring finger over the saphenous opening (femoral). In the invagination test the tip suggests indirect and the pulp direct. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You attached the scrotal swelling to the direct hernia, the one that sounds more severe. The indirect sac follows the cord down the canal: pear-shaped, often reaching the scrotum, reducing up, lateral and back. The direct hernia is globular, near the pubic tubercle, reduces straight back and rarely reaches the scrotum. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You filed both triangles as 'no-tack zones' and swapped their contents. Doom lies between the vas deferens and gonadal vessels and holds the external iliac vessels. Pain lies lateral to the gonadal vessels, below the iliopubic tract, and holds the lateral femoral cutaneous, genitofemoral branch and femoral nerves. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You gave the femoral hernia the inguinal position. An inguinal hernia emerges above and medial to the pubic tubercle; a femoral hernia lies below and lateral. Anchor the femoral neck below the inguinal ligament, and the position will stop being copied across. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You first swapped lateral and medial, then fixed it by following each sac's route: the indirect sac enters at the deep ring lateral to the vessels, the direct sac bulges through the posterior wall medial to them. Under exam pressure this trap can return, so recheck it in the review card.

You hold Hesselbach's triangle as a list of landmarks near the direct hernia, so rings and Cooper's ligament slip in. Rebuild it from three sides: inferior epigastric artery, lateral rectus border, inguinal ligament. Exam keys use the inguinal ligament as the base, though the original description used Cooper's. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You first read femoral hernia as the commonest in women, then separated a relative skew from a ranking: indirect inguinal still leads. Under exam pressure this trap can return, so recheck it in the review card.

You carried the reducible-hernia habit of pushing it back into a case where the bowel may be dead. Forceful taxis can push gangrenous bowel back or cause reduction en masse. With a tense, tender, toxic presentation, the first step is resuscitation and emergency surgery. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You picked tests by sophistication. A clinically evident hernia needs no imaging. Ultrasound is the first test for an occult hernia, MRI the step after an inconclusive ultrasound, and CT is kept for complicated or obscure cases. Ask evident, occult or complicated before choosing. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You started with the older Bassini key, then learned both: older PYQs expected Bassini, current practice is Lichtenstein mesh repair. Under exam pressure this trap can return, so recheck it in the review card.

You placed the conjoint tendon beside internal oblique, so on the anterior wall. The anterior wall is external oblique aponeurosis, reinforced laterally by internal oblique. The posterior wall is transversalis fascia, reinforced medially by the conjoint tendon. Place structures by the wall they reinforce. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.

You assumed direct and indirect differ only in position, so you swapped their causes. Indirect hernia is congenital, from a patent processus vaginalis; direct is acquired, from posterior wall weakness. Complete persistence of the processus gives a congenital hernia reaching the testis, partial gives a funicular hernia. You may have fixed it on the spot, but that does not show it holds. Meet it again on a fresh question: do its review card next.
You swapped Amyand and de Garengeot, then anchored each to its site: Amyand inguinal, de Garengeot femoral. Under exam pressure this trap can return, so recheck it in the review card.
You tend to get a direction backwards, such as lateral versus medial, or what a test blocks. Predict the route first, then pick the answer.
You tend to skip qualifiers such as child versus adult, groin versus inguinal, open versus laparoscopic. Underline the qualifier before reading the options.
You tend to mismatch eponyms and associations: fingers, causes, triangles or appendix hernias. Practise them as paired recall with the discriminating feature.
You tend to mix up look-alike pairs, such as direct versus indirect pictures or the three operation terms. Next time, name the one feature that separates them before choosing.
You tapped Sure on more than one answer that turned out wrong. Those are the errors that survive revision, so review them first and treat a Sure tap as a prompt to check the qualifier.
You asked for hints or explanations several times. That is fine, but try the next review card cold, answering before looking, so the report can show what you recall unaided.
You skipped a lesson with the fast lane. Skipping is allowed, but the report cannot tell whether you knew that material, so do the review cards for the skipped lesson to check it holds.
Do the review cards in the order listed: confident errors first, then gaps, then shaky areas. Retry the journey after a day, and tackle one gap per sitting.
